origin:
Garage 59 emerged from the passion of Andrew Kirkaldy, a successful GT racer with a vision. Frustrated by the limitations of solely driving, Kirkaldy sought to build a team that blended professional expertise with the camaraderie of amateur racing. In 2014, Garage 59 was founded, initially focusing on McLaren GT machinery. The early days saw the team competing in various GT series across Europe, learning the ropes and building a foundation for future success. A pivotal moment came in 2016, when they secured a surprise podium finish at the Blancpain GT Series Endurance Cup race at Monza, proving their potential against more established professional outfits.

The team's early successes attracted investment, allowing them to upgrade their equipment and expand their racing program. Garage 59 quickly established itself as a competitive force in the amateur GT racing scene, attracting talented drivers and experienced engineers. They've consistently punched above their weight, challenging professional teams with their dedication and strategic approach to racing.
philosophy: Garage 59's philosophy centers around a driver-centric approach, prioritizing the development and support of their amateur drivers. They believe in fostering a positive and collaborative team environment, where every member feels valued and empowered. Car development is approached methodically, focusing on incremental improvements and data-driven analysis to extract maximum performance from their machinery. They value reliability as much as outright speed, understanding that consistent finishes are crucial for championship success.

teamPrincipal.name: Andrew Kirkaldy
teamPrincipal.background: A former professional GT racer himself, Andrew Kirkaldy brings a wealth of experience and a deep understanding of the sport to his role as Team Principal. He is known for his calm demeanor, strategic thinking, and ability to motivate his team.

keyFigures.name: Bas Leinders
keyFigures.description: A former Formula 1 test driver and experienced GT racer, Bas Leinders oversees the team's sporting operations, ensuring smooth execution and strategic decision-making during race weekends.

keyFigures.name: James Murphy
keyFigures.description: James Murphy is responsible for the technical direction of the team, overseeing car setup, data analysis, and performance optimization. He has a keen eye for detail and a passion for extracting every last bit of performance from the team's machinery.

headquarters: Garage 59 operates from a modest workshop in Silverstone, UK. While the facilities are basic, they are well-equipped for maintaining and preparing their GT cars. The team also utilizes external resources for advanced testing and simulation.
fanBase: Garage 59 enjoys a loyal following among amateur racing enthusiasts, who appreciate their underdog spirit and commitment to fair play. Their fans are drawn to the team's accessible atmosphere and the opportunity to witness amateur drivers competing against professionals.
